tagline: A dense, working-class district at the crossroads of old Istanbul — international food, the city's best offal restaurants, and non-stop street life.

items.name: Laleli Kahvaltı Salonları
items.description: Traditional Turkish breakfast houses around Laleli and Aksaray, catering to traders and early risers. Simple, filling, and very inexpensive.

items.name: Uluslararası Kahveler (Aksaray)
items.description: The international community in Aksaray has brought excellent Central Asian and Middle Eastern tea houses. A different Istanbul entirely.

items.name: İşkembeci Restoranları
items.description: Aksaray is famous for its tripe and offal restaurants — a true local Istanbul institution. Open late into the night.
items.tip: İşkembe çorbası (tripe soup) at midnight is a classic Istanbul experience. An acquired taste, but the real deal.

items.name: Laleli Tekstil Bölgesi Lokantalari
items.description: The streets around Laleli's textile market are packed with no-frills lokanta restaurants serving traders. Rotating menus, huge portions, tiny prices.

items.name: Uygur ve Orta Asya Mutfağı
items.description: Aksaray has a significant Uyghur and Central Asian community — hand-pulled noodles, laghman, and Central Asian bread unlike anywhere else in Istanbul.
items.tip: Ask locals which Uyghur restaurant is currently best — the scene changes. Look for hand-pulled noodles (laghman) on the menu.

items.name: Laleli Çarşısı
items.description: The wholesale textile and fashion market of Istanbul. Huge quantities of clothing, fabrics, and leather goods at trade prices. The atmosphere is chaotic and fascinating.

items.name: Aksaray Meydanı
items.description: A busy, non-touristy central square that functions as one of the major transit hubs of the city. Observing everyday Istanbul life at full intensity.

tips: Aksaray is a major transit junction — the M1A/M1B metro and the T1 tram meet here, with the M2 and Marmaray one stop away at Yenikapı.
This is one of the most ethnically diverse neighbourhoods in Istanbul — Arabic, Uyghur, African, and many more communities coexist.
Not a tourist destination, but a fascinating window into how Istanbul actually functions. Go curious, not cautious.
The area around Laleli is known for wholesale shopping — many traders from Russia, Central Asia, and the Middle East come specifically for this.
